en.statement: Artificial intelligence sits within machine learning in the hierarchy of AI technologies.
en.explanation: Machine learning is one branch of AI. AI also includes approaches that use explicitly programmed reasoning.

source.title: What is Machine Learning?

en.statement: A deep learning image classifier needs engineers to specify features such as ear and tail shape before training.
en.explanation: Deep learning performs feature engineering with minimal human intervention. Manually configuring features such as ear or tail shape is typical of traditional ML.

source.title: Deep Learning vs Machine Learning

en.statement: Supervised learning requires training examples paired with the target answers a model learns to predict.
en.explanation: The target labels provide feedback about the expected result, helping the model learn relationships between inputs and outcomes.

source.title: What Is Supervised Learning?

en.statement: Unsupervised learning discovers which products customers tend to purchase together.
en.explanation: Association analysis finds co-occurrence patterns in purchase records, such as items that frequently appear in the same basket.

source.title: What Is Unsupervised Learning?

en.statement: Reinforcement learning favors the next immediate reward over rewards accumulated across a task.
en.explanation: Reinforcement learning seeks cumulative reward. It can learn actions whose benefits arrive later in a task.

source.title: What is Reinforcement Learning?

en.statement: Inference adjusts a trained model's learned weights to fit the new input it receives.
en.explanation: Inference applies an already trained model to an input to produce a prediction. The learning of model weights belongs to training.

source.title: Deploy models for inference

en.statement: Deep neural networks need far more training examples than traditional machine learning methods.
en.explanation: Deep networks have many layers and weights to learn, so they need millions of training examples rather than the hundreds or thousands a simpler network might need.

source.title: What is a Neural Network?

en.statement: A trained ML model is the learning procedure that discovers patterns in training data.
en.explanation: In machine learning, you use an algorithm and example data to train a model, then integrate the trained model into an application to generate inferences.

source.title: Overview of machine learning with Amazon SageMaker AI

en.statement: Computer vision object detection reports where multiple objects appear within the same image.
en.explanation: Object detection locates individual objects within an image, which helps a vision system distinguish objects appearing in different positions.

source.title: What is Computer Vision?

en.statement: Amazon Textract extracts form fields and table cells from scanned business documents.
en.explanation: Amazon Textract recovers structured data from forms and tables, which helps automate entry of business records.

source.title: What is Amazon Textract?

en.statement: Amazon Transcribe can identify a meeting speaker's real name through speaker diarization.
en.explanation: Amazon Transcribe assigns anonymous speaker labels to separate voices in a transcript. Diarization distinguishes speakers rather than verifying their identities.

source.title: Partitioning speakers (diarization)

en.statement: Amazon Lex uses a slot to represent the user's goal, such as booking a hotel.
en.explanation: An intent represents the user's requested action in Amazon Lex. A slot supplies a detail needed for that action, such as the travel date.

source.title: Amazon Lex V2 core concepts

en.statement: Amazon Rekognition decides if an image meets a company's content policy from its moderation labels.
en.explanation: Amazon Rekognition reports moderation categories and confidence. The application owner applies business rules to decide whether the image is acceptable.

source.title: Using the image and video moderation APIs

en.statement: Amazon Translate sets whether a translation sounds formal or informal through its custom terminology feature.
en.explanation: Custom terminology controls translations of specific terms, such as brand names. The formality setting controls how formal the translated text sounds.

source.title: Customizing your translations with Amazon Translate

en.statement: Amazon Personalize can update recommendations as a retailer records a user's recent item interactions.
en.explanation: For supported use cases, Amazon Personalize uses recorded interactions to adapt recommendations to a user's changing interests.

source.title: Recording real-time events to influence recommendations

en.statement: A retailer uses regression to predict a customer's next order value as a numerical amount.
en.explanation: Regression, called numeric prediction in SageMaker Canvas, predicts a numeric target such as a price or an order value rather than a category.

source.title: How custom models work

en.statement: A rules-based baseline sets the bar an ML solution must beat to justify its added cost.
en.explanation: A business compares ML with simpler alternatives to justify its additional cost and complexity. Existing rules provide a useful baseline for that comparison.

source.title: MLCOST02-BP01 Identify if machine learning is the right solution

en.statement: When a lender must show how each credit decision is made, AWS guidance favors a decision tree over a complex model.
en.explanation: The Responsible AI Lens recommends interpretable models such as decision trees or linear models when explanations are critical, adding post-hoc explanation tools only when a complex model is required.

source.title: RAISP02-BP07 Incorporate explainability mechanisms into the core AI system

en.statement: SageMaker Canvas gives business analysts a visual workflow for training predictive models.
en.explanation: SageMaker Canvas offers a no-code workflow for building custom predictive models from business data.

source.title: Amazon SageMaker Canvas

en.statement: SageMaker Feature Store's online store keeps historical versions of records for model training.
en.explanation: The online store retains the latest feature records for low-latency predictions. The offline store keeps historical records for training.

source.title: Create, store, and share features with Feature Store

en.statement: SageMaker Model Registry tracks the approval status of model versions considered for production.
en.explanation: SageMaker Model Registry records model versions and their approval status, helping teams control which versions advance toward deployment.

source.title: Model Registration Deployment with Model Registry

en.statement: A model needing GPU inference fits an Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoint rather than a serverless one.
en.explanation: Serverless Inference excludes GPUs, along with features such as VPC configuration and multi-model endpoints, so a GPU-backed model runs on an instance-based endpoint such as a real-time one.

source.title: Deploy models with Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference

en.statement: On-demand Amazon SageMaker AI serverless endpoints keep compute warm through idle periods.
en.explanation: On-demand serverless endpoints scale down during idle periods. A later request can encounter a cold start while compute starts up.

source.title: Deploy models with Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference

en.statement: Amazon SageMaker AI batch transform requires a persistent endpoint to process an offline dataset.
en.explanation: Batch transform runs prediction jobs over datasets rather than serving requests through a persistent inference endpoint.

source.title: Batch transform for inference with Amazon SageMaker AI

en.statement: In MLOps, a change in incoming data is one of the events that triggers a pipeline to re-train and redeploy a model.
en.explanation: MLOps automates model training and deployment, with pipeline runs triggered by data changes, code changes, monitoring or calendar events, so a model is refreshed repeatably.

source.title: What is MLOps?

en.statement: Data drift describes the decline in a deployed model's prediction accuracy as time passes.
en.explanation: Data drift is a change in the distribution of input data compared with the data used as a baseline.

source.title: MLREL03-BP03 Validate models with relevant data

en.statement: Precision measures the share of actual positive cases that a classifier successfully detects.
en.explanation: Precision measures how many predicted positive cases are actually positive. It helps assess the reliability of positive predictions.

source.title: Metrics and validation

en.statement: A text model counts the words in a prompt to determine its number of input tokens.
en.explanation: Text tokens may be parts of words, complete words or punctuation. Counting written words therefore gives a different measure from counting tokens.

source.title: Key terminology

en.statement: Text embeddings place passages with similar meanings close together in a numerical vector space.
en.explanation: An embedding captures relationships in a numerical representation. Similarity between text vectors reflects similarity in their meaning.

source.title: What are Embeddings in Machine Learning?

en.statement: RAG ingestion converts each document chunk into its own embedding vector.
en.explanation: RAG ingestion splits documents into chunks, converts each chunk to an embedding and writes it to a vector index, keeping a mapping back to the original document.

source.title: How Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases work

en.statement: An MCP host shares one MCP client across its connections to several MCP servers.
en.explanation: An MCP host creates a separate client for a server connection. The host coordinates these clients as it connects to multiple servers.

source.title: Architecture overview

en.statement: A transformer's attention weighs relationships between distant parts of an input sequence.
en.explanation: Attention gives relevant parts of a sequence greater influence. It helps a transformer interpret meaning using context located farther away.

source.title: What are Transformers in Artificial Intelligence?

en.statement: A diffusion model creates an image by progressively adding noise to a clean image.
en.explanation: During image generation, a diffusion model removes noise to construct the requested image. Adding noise belongs to the forward process used in training.

source.title: What Is a Diffusion Model?

en.statement: Context engineering centers on improving the wording of a single user prompt.
en.explanation: Context engineering assembles relevant information for the current task, such as conversation history and tool information, into an LLM's context.

source.title: Understanding context engineering for generative AI

en.statement: MCP connects AI applications to external systems through a model-provider-specific interface.
en.explanation: The Model Context Protocol standardizes connections to external tools, data and workflows. Its interface works across a broad ecosystem of AI applications.

source.title: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?

en.statement: MCP servers expose reusable prompt templates, such as few-shot examples, as a primitive.
en.explanation: MCP defines three server primitives: tools are functions an AI application invokes, resources supply context data, and prompts are reusable templates such as system prompts or few-shot examples.

source.title: Architecture overview

en.statement: An LLM can present fabricated information in a polished answer that sounds confident and convincing.
en.explanation: An LLM can hallucinate facts while producing fluent, confident text. Plausible language is one way fabricated information can mislead users.

source.title: What is Retrieval-Augmented Generation?

en.statement: A fixed prompt makes a foundation model's repeated answers identical across separate requests.
en.explanation: LLM generation is probabilistic, so an unchanged prompt can produce different answers on repeated requests.

source.title: Prompt engineering concepts

en.statement: A pre-trained model updates its learned knowledge when a news website publishes a new story.
en.explanation: A model's learned knowledge reflects its training data and cutoff. Publishing a new webpage does not itself update that learned knowledge.

source.title: What is Retrieval-Augmented Generation?

en.statement: Image input support implies that a foundation model supports image generation in its responses.
en.explanation: A foundation model's accepted inputs and generated outputs are separate capabilities. A model that accepts images may return text rather than generated pictures.

source.title: Inference using Invoke API

en.statement: One foundation model handles question answering, translation and code generation through its prompts.
en.explanation: Unlike traditional ML models built for one specific task, a foundation model performs a wide range of disparate tasks based on its input prompts, which gives generative AI its adaptability.

source.title: What are Foundation Models?

en.statement: User-perceived time to first token in a RAG assistant counts context retrieval time.
en.explanation: AWS splits user-perceived time to first token into pre-stream work (input processing, context retrieval, prompt construction) and model inference time, so slow retrieval delays the first token.

source.title: Definitions - Agentic AI Lens

en.statement: Between two foundation models, the one with more parameters gives higher accuracy on a company's specialist task.
en.explanation: Parameter count describes model size, not task fit. AWS advises benchmarking candidate models on the workload's own tasks, since a model that leads a general benchmark can underperform there.

source.title: AGENTPERF02-BP02 Implement task-appropriate model selection strategies

en.statement: A generative AI ownership-cost estimate includes staff education for overseeing model-generated work.
en.explanation: Generative AI ownership costs include educating the people who use and manage the application. That expense sits outside the model's inference bill.

source.title: Optimizing Cost for Generative AI with AWS

en.statement: A foundation model keeps generated creative writing unique to the customer who requests it.
en.explanation: A foundation model's creative output may overlap with output it independently produces for another customer. Requesting original prose does not establish exclusive wording.

source.title: Prompt engineering concepts

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock gives teams the same control over model-training infrastructure as Amazon SageMaker AI.
en.explanation: Amazon Bedrock manages the infrastructure used for its foundation models. Amazon SageMaker AI offers training jobs and hosting with greater infrastructure control.

source.title: Amazon Bedrock or Amazon SageMaker AI?

en.statement: Teams use Amazon Nova foundation models through Amazon Bedrock for generative AI applications.
en.explanation: Amazon Nova supplies Amazon's foundation models. Applications send inputs to Amazon Bedrock and receive responses from the selected Nova model.

source.title: What is Amazon Nova 2?

en.statement: Amazon Quick connects company knowledge with actions in the business applications an organization uses.
en.explanation: Quick uses organizational data connections and action connectors to carry out business work in connected applications.

source.title: What is Amazon Quick?

en.statement: Kiro steering files keep project conventions for the current chat session and discard them when it ends.
en.explanation: Steering files are markdown files in a workspace .kiro/steering folder or a global one. Kiro loads them into later interactions, so project conventions persist across chats.

source.title: Steering

en.statement: Strands Agents uses a developer-defined execution order to coordinate agents in a swarm.
en.explanation: In a Strands Agents swarm, agents decide when to hand work to other agents. A fixed execution sequence belongs to a workflow pattern.

source.title: Multi-agent patterns

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime separates user sessions to protect an agent's in-memory working state.
en.explanation: AgentCore Runtime isolates session memory so one user's stateful agent execution stays separate from another user's session.

source.title: Host agent or tools with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock bills Provisioned Throughput by the tokens processed during active requests.
en.explanation: Provisioned Throughput is billed per hour for the model units purchased until it is deleted. A 1-month or 6-month commitment lowers the hourly price; a no-commitment option also exists.

source.title: Increase model invocation capacity with Provisioned Throughput in Amazon Bedrock

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock batch inference lowers charges for eligible workloads compared with on-demand inference.
en.explanation: AWS prices eligible batch workloads below on-demand inference. The chosen model's batch pricing determines whether that cost advantage applies.

source.title: Amazon Bedrock Pricing

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock's Flex tier trades longer processing times for lower inference charges.
en.explanation: The Flex tier discounts inference for workloads that tolerate longer processing. Its cost advantage comes with a response-time trade-off.

source.title: Service tiers for optimizing performance and cost

en.statement: Lowering a foundation model's temperature produces a wider variety of responses to the same prompt.
en.explanation: Lower temperature favors more probable outputs, reducing response variation. This makes repeated responses more consistent.

source.title: Influence response generation with inference parameters

en.statement: Top P restricts a foundation model's next-token choice to a fixed number of candidate tokens.
en.explanation: Top P selects candidate tokens by their cumulative probability mass. The number of candidates depends on the model's probability distribution.

source.title: Influence response generation with inference parameters

en.statement: A RAG application adds retrieved source information to a model's prompt when a user asks a question.
en.explanation: Retrieval supplies relevant source material while the application answers the query. The model uses that material as context for its response.

source.title: How Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases works

en.statement: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL stores foundation model embeddings through the pgvector extension.
en.explanation: The pgvector extension adds vector storage and similarity search to PostgreSQL. Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL offers it for AI applications that use embeddings.

source.title: Vector database options

en.statement: Prompt caching in Amazon Bedrock reuses completed answers when users repeat a question.
en.explanation: Amazon Bedrock prompt caching reuses shared input context. Reusing that context reduces the model's repeated input processing on later requests.

source.title: Prompt caching

en.statement: The Well-Architected Generative AI Lens advises fine-tuning an FM before trying RAG to keep adaptation costs low.
en.explanation: The Well-Architected Generative AI Lens says to start with prompt engineering, then evaluate RAG, and move to fine-tuning only if needed, to cut time, cost and complexity.

source.title: GENOPS05-BP01 Learn when to customize models

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory extracts user preferences from earlier conversations for later interactions.
en.explanation: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory stores useful insights from past interactions in long-term memory. Agents use those insights to personalize later conversations.

source.title: Add memory to your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway turns existing APIs into MCP-compatible tools for agents.
en.explanation: Gateway translates an agent's MCP requests into calls to underlying APIs. Existing services become usable as tools through this managed gateway.

source.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway: A secure AI gateway for agents, tools, and models

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Code Interpreter performs numerical analysis in an isolated sandbox.
en.explanation: Agents use the service for computational tasks where model reasoning alone falls short. Its sandbox separates code execution from the agent application.

source.title: Execute code and analyze data using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Code Interpreter

en.statement: A system-level persona instruction guides an FM's response style across later conversation turns.
en.explanation: A system prompt sets the response persona for the conversation. That instruction continues guiding follow-up responses rather than serving as a one-turn user request.

source.title: Using the system role

en.statement: Chain-of-thought prompting raises an FM's output tokens and latency versus asking for a direct answer.
en.explanation: Writing out intermediate reasoning adds output tokens and time before the answer, so AWS suggests chain-of-thought for multistep analysis, math and complex reasoning rather than simple tasks.

source.title: Give Amazon Nova time to think (chain-of-thought)

en.statement: Negative prompting can steer an LLM away from confusing document classes with similar characteristics.
en.explanation: A prompt describes classification mistakes to avoid when document types are easy to confuse. This guides the model away from mixing up similar labels.

source.title: How Myriad Genetics achieved fast, accurate, and cost-efficient document processing using the AWS open-source Generative AI Intelligent Document Processing Accelerator

en.statement: In Prompt management in Amazon Bedrock, an FM supplies the values for a prompt template's variables.
en.explanation: The caller supplies request-specific values for prompt variables when testing or running the prompt. The template reuses its instructions with that supplied data.

source.title: Construct and store reusable prompts with Prompt management in Amazon Bedrock

en.statement: Labeled delimiters enforce a security boundary between an FM's reference text and task instructions.
en.explanation: Delimiters organize a prompt's sections, but an attacker can spoof the tags and insert harmful instructions. Treat the labels as formatting cues rather than enforced security controls.

source.title: Common prompt injection attacks

en.statement: Packing a prompt with as much background detail as possible makes a foundation model's answers more precise.
en.explanation: AWS advises balancing simplicity and complexity in a prompt: one that is too simple may lack context, while one that is too complex may confuse the model and lead to vague or unexpected answers.

source.title: What is Prompt Engineering?

en.statement: Jailbreaking targets an FM's built-in safety training, while prompt injection targets developer instructions.
en.explanation: In AWS's prompt attack taxonomy, jailbreaks try to bypass the model's native safety and moderation, while prompt injections try to ignore and override instructions the developer set.

source.title: Detect prompt attacks with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

en.statement: Data poisoning threatens an FM application through its RAG knowledge base as well as through its training data.
en.explanation: AWS lists data poisoning of training or operational data sources among AI security threats, and names RAG knowledge bases among the operational datasets that may be compromised.

source.title: RAIBR02-BP06 Identify potential harmful events impacting system and data security

en.statement: Prompt management in Amazon Bedrock changes a saved version when a developer edits its working draft.
en.explanation: A prompt version preserves a snapshot of the prompt and its configuration at creation time. A developer continues editing the working draft while the saved version retains that snapshot.

source.title: Deploy a prompt to your application using versions in Prompt management

en.statement: Self-supervised pre-training derives prediction targets directly from a language model's input text.
en.explanation: A language model learns from patterns in its text corpus, such as predicting the next token from preceding text. The training text supplies the target as well as the context.

source.title: What are Foundation Models?

en.statement: Continued pre-training adapts an FM using labeled examples of tasks paired with their desired answers.
en.explanation: Continued pre-training extends pre-training with additional unlabeled domain text. Labeled input-output pairs belong to supervised fine-tuning.

source.title: Continued pre-training (CPT)

en.statement: Instruction tuning helps a model apply learned task patterns to instructions absent from its training examples.
en.explanation: Training across varied instruction-based tasks improves general instruction following. A model uses related learned concepts when it encounters a new task prompt.

source.title: Zero-shot prompting for the Flan-T5 foundation model in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart

en.statement: Transfer learning typically keeps a model's task-specific final layers and retrains its earlier general layers.
en.explanation: In most models the last layers are task-specific, so transfer learning removes or retrains them and keeps the earlier layers that hold general knowledge.

source.title: What is Transfer Learning?

en.statement: Model distillation transfers a teacher model's learned weights directly to a smaller student model.
en.explanation: A student learns from response examples produced by a teacher. Distillation passes behavioral knowledge through training data rather than copying the teacher's weights.

source.title: Customize a model with distillation in Amazon Bedrock

en.statement: RLHF trains its reward model to reproduce ideal answers written by human reviewers.
en.explanation: An RLHF reward model learns to score responses according to human preferences. Its scores guide training toward behavior that people prefer.

source.title: Fine-tune large language models with reinforcement learning from human or AI feedback

en.statement: A large fine-tuning dataset of uneven quality usually beats a smaller, carefully curated one.
en.explanation: Quality beats quantity in fine-tuning data: a small set of carefully curated examples can match models trained on far more data, and keeping only the cleanest examples can score higher.

source.title: Preparing data for supervised fine-tuning Part 1: Formatting and quality

en.statement: Narrow domain fine-tuning exposes an FM to the risk of losing its earlier task capabilities.
en.explanation: Catastrophic forgetting occurs when new training overwrites useful prior capabilities. Domain specialization can therefore reduce performance outside the new training focus.

source.title: Preparing data for supervised fine-tuning Part 2: Advanced data strategies

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock's reinforcement fine-tuning accepts recorded invocation prompts as training data.
en.explanation: Amazon Bedrock offers invocation logs as a training data source for reinforcement fine-tuning. Recorded requests supply prompts drawn from the application's actual usage.

source.title: Customize a model with reinforcement fine-tuning in Amazon Bedrock

en.statement: ROUGE evaluates a generated summary's readability by comparing it with a reference summary.
en.explanation: ROUGE checks words or word sequences shared by generated and reference summaries. It measures content overlap rather than readability or coherent phrasing.

source.title: Evaluate the text summarization capabilities of LLMs for enhanced decision-making on AWS

en.statement: BERTScore recognizes similarity between a generated summary and a reference that uses different wording.
en.explanation: BERTScore compares contextual embeddings of tokens in generated and reference text. It credits similar meaning expressed through synonyms or paraphrases.

source.title: Evaluate the text summarization capabilities of LLMs for enhanced decision-making on AWS

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock judge-based evaluations return a score per response and leave explaining it to human reviewers.
en.explanation: A judge-based evaluation uses a second model, the evaluator, to score each generator response against the selected metrics and to write an explanation of every score.

source.title: Evaluate model performance using another LLM as a judge

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock programmatic evaluations accept a custom prompt dataset instead of a built-in one.
en.explanation: Programmatic evaluation jobs run on a built-in dataset or on a prompt dataset tailored to your use case, so the scores reflect the tasks your application handles.

source.title: Evaluate the performance of Amazon Bedrock resources

en.statement: Test cases drawn from a model's fine-tuning data give a reliable measure of its performance on new inputs.
en.explanation: Evaluation data stays separate from training and fine-tuning data. A model has already seen its tuning examples, so scores on them overstate how it handles new inputs.

source.title: RAIDP01-BP02 Identify the datasets needed for training and customizing your system

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock automatic evaluations use different accuracy measures for summarization and question answering.
en.explanation: Amazon Bedrock selects accuracy measures suited to the generation task. An accuracy result needs interpretation in the context of the task being evaluated.

source.title: Model evaluation task types in Amazon Bedrock

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock retrieve-only RAG evaluations score the final answer written by a response generator.
en.explanation: Amazon Bedrock evaluates retrieval quality from the retrieved information. A retrieve-only evaluation isolates that stage; response-generation quality belongs to the combined evaluation.

source.title: Evaluate the performance of RAG sources using Amazon Bedrock evaluations

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations scores tool choices in the context of an agent's conversation.
en.explanation: AgentCore Evaluations assesses whether the selected tool serves the user's request at that point in the conversation, using the available tools and preceding context.

source.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore built-in evaluator prompt templates

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations judges an agent's goal success from one tool call rather than the whole session.
en.explanation: The goal success rate evaluator is session-level: it reviews the whole conversation to decide whether the agent completed all of the user's goals.

source.title: Prompt templates - Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

en.statement: AI teams select fairness criteria independently of the use case and affected stakeholders.
en.explanation: AI teams choose fairness criteria for the use case and affected stakeholders. Different fairness goals can conflict, so the choice depends on context.

source.title: Measure fairness as unwanted bias across stakeholder groups

en.statement: AI robustness includes a model's behavior on adversarial inputs designed to mislead its predictions.
en.explanation: Robustness concerns useful, reliable outputs under unexpected or adversarial inputs. Performance on ordinary inputs leaves this behavior untested.

source.title: Responsible AI: From principles to practice

en.statement: Label quality checks compare how each annotator labels different demographic groups to detect human bias.
en.explanation: AWS advises hunting for annotator bias, such as one annotator consistently labeling some groups differently than others, as part of validating label quality.

source.title: RAIDP02-BP03 Validate the quality of human and generated labels and features in your dataset

en.statement: AI teams infer demographic groups' error rates from a model's combined population-wide error rate.
en.explanation: A population-wide error rate can conceal differences between demographic groups. Subgroup analysis examines performance separately for relevant groups.

source.title: Measure fairness as unwanted bias across stakeholder groups

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails can check both user text and model responses for harmful content.
en.explanation: Content filters examine input prompts and model responses for harmful content such as hate or violence. Filtering strength is configurable for the application's needs.

source.title: Create your guardrail

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails uses AWS's fixed list of denied topics for a banking assistant.
en.explanation: Customers define denied topics for their application's boundaries, such as investment advice for a banking assistant. The topic definition guides detection.

source.title: Block denied topics to help remove harmful content

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails word filters can block synonyms of a configured phrase through semantic similarity.
en.explanation: Custom word filters match configured words and phrases exactly. A paraphrase or synonym needs its own matching entry to be blocked by that filter.

source.title: Remove a specific list of words and phrases from conversations with word filters

en.statement: AI teams choose smaller models that meet their quality needs to reduce the workload's energy demand.
en.explanation: Right-sized models reduce unnecessary computational work while meeting the task's quality needs. Model selection therefore affects the environmental footprint of inference.

source.title: Leverage smaller models and optimized inference techniques to reduce carbon footprint

en.statement: Model-generated content can expose a business to copyright infringement claims when it uses the output.
en.explanation: Copyright claims can concern generated output, even when an AI model creates it. AI generation alone does not clear the rights of third parties.

source.title: Amazon Bedrock FAQs

en.statement: SHAP assigns the probability that a model's predicted outcome is correct for the input it receives.
en.explanation: SHAP estimates how input features contribute to a model's output relative to a baseline. These attributions describe influence rather than a prediction's probability of being correct.

source.title: What is Explainable AI?

en.statement: Local explanations describe the factors driving a model's predictions across a customer population.
en.explanation: Local explanations address an individual prediction. Global explanations summarize a model's behavior across multiple predictions.

source.title: What is Explainable AI?

en.statement: A post-hoc surrogate explanation directly reveals the original model's internal decision rules.
en.explanation: A post-hoc surrogate approximates a model's input-output behavior. Its simplified rules describe that approximation rather than recovering the model's actual internal rules.

source.title: What is Explainable AI?

en.statement: AWS guidance flags stronger privacy protection as a criterion that competes with explaining AI decisions.
en.explanation: Release criteria can conflict: stronger privacy protections can make it harder to explain how decisions are made, so AWS advises meeting a minimum target for each criterion.

source.title: RAISP01-BP02 Consider design trade-offs across competing objectives

en.statement: Developers use SageMaker Model Cards to record suitable production uses of a machine learning model.
en.explanation: SageMaker Model Cards document the scenarios a model suits, development assumptions, and uses its developers discourage. This guides responsible adoption.

source.title: Amazon SageMaker Model Cards

en.statement: AWS AI Service Cards certify that a customer's AI application meets its fairness requirements.
en.explanation: AWS AI Service Cards explain intended uses, limitations, and responsible design choices for services and models. Customers assess their own application against its fairness requirements.

source.title: Responsible AI Tools and Resources

en.statement: Public access to a model's weights allows a business to use the model commercially.
en.explanation: A model's license governs permitted use. Public availability does not establish commercial permission; users need to check the provider's applicable terms for their use case.

source.title: Model sources and license agreements

en.statement: A counterfactual explanation shows what input edits would make a model return a different decision.
en.explanation: Counterfactual explanations identify a small input change that changes a model's prediction. For a loan model, the alternative might involve a different income value.

source.title: Machine Learning Best Practices in Healthcare and Life Sciences: Model interpretability

en.statement: Human-centered AI design includes channels through which users challenge a model's decisions.
en.explanation: Feedback mechanisms let users contest AI outcomes after receiving them. This gives affected people a route to question and improve the system's behavior.

source.title: Map the user journey to identify AI interaction requirements

en.statement: Under the shared responsibility model, AWS prevents prompt injection in a customer's Amazon Bedrock application.
en.explanation: Customers prevent prompt injection in their Amazon Bedrock applications. AWS secures the underlying infrastructure and the Bedrock service; application-level protections remain the customer's responsibility.

source.title: Prompt injection security

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails can replace detected personal information with placeholders in a model response.
en.explanation: Sensitive information filters redact detected personal information when configured to mask it. Placeholders indicate the information type while preserving the surrounding response text.

source.title: Remove PII from conversations by using sensitive information filters

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails contextual grounding checks validate responses against customer-defined logical rules.
en.explanation: Contextual grounding checks compare a response with source information and the user query. Automated Reasoning checks validate responses against logical rules and policies that customers define.

source.title: Create your guardrail

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity manages credentials for an agent to access external services on a user's behalf.
en.explanation: AgentCore Identity provides credential management for authorized access to third-party tools and services. An agent uses this managed access to perform work on behalf of a user.

source.title: Provide identity and credential management for agent applications with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity

en.statement: Policy in AgentCore delegates decisions about a tool call's authorization to the agent's foundation model.
en.explanation: Policy in AgentCore evaluates tool requests against deterministic policies at the Gateway boundary. Enforcement takes place outside the agent, before it receives access to the requested tool.

source.title: Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: Control Agent Interactions

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock can improve its base models using prompts submitted by its customers.
en.explanation: Amazon Bedrock's data-use commitment excludes customer content from improving its base models. This protection applies to prompts submitted to the service.

source.title: Amazon Bedrock FAQs

en.statement: A RAG application's similarity search automatically enforces users' permissions on confidential documents.
en.explanation: RAG retrieval needs access controls based on the user's permissions. Semantic similarity determines relevance, while permission checks determine which documents the user may receive.

source.title: Implement least privilege access permissions for foundation models accessing data stores

en.statement: Amazon Macie automatically flags sensitive data it detects in AI training datasets stored in Amazon S3.
en.explanation: Amazon Macie generates findings when it discovers sensitive information in analyzed S3 objects. AI teams use these findings to locate training data that needs privacy protection.

source.title: What is Amazon Macie?

en.statement: Data lineage traces an AI dataset's origins and the transformations recorded along its processing path.
en.explanation: Lineage records the provenance and transformation history of data used by an AI system. Teams consult this history to investigate data quality issues and demonstrate how the data was handled.

source.title: Providing secure access to data and systems for generative AI

en.statement: Encryption of the network connection between an AI application and Amazon Bedrock is handled by AWS KMS.
en.explanation: Requests to the Amazon Bedrock API travel over a secure SSL/TLS connection, while AWS KMS manages the keys that encrypt stored resources such as custom models and evaluation jobs.

source.title: Data encryption

en.statement: AWS CloudTrail can give AI auditors point-in-time configuration snapshots of a training-data bucket.
en.explanation: AWS Config records resource configurations at particular times. AWS CloudTrail records actions and caller information, which helps auditors investigate who changed the resource.

source.title: AWS Config FAQs

en.statement: AWS Trusted Advisor gives AI auditors AWS's compliance audit reports as evidence of provider controls.
en.explanation: AWS Artifact supplies AWS's security and compliance reports. AWS Trusted Advisor checks resource usage and configuration against best practices.

source.title: Choosing an AWS cloud governance service

en.statement: Amazon Inspector scans software packages on Amazon EC2 instances hosting AI models for known vulnerabilities.
en.explanation: Package vulnerability findings identify affected software and known exposures. This helps teams assess vulnerabilities in the software running their model-hosting instances.

source.title: Amazon Inspector finding types

en.statement: Amazon Bedrock cross-Region inference lets an AI team restrict processing to an approved geography.
en.explanation: A Geographic profile routes requests inside its specified geography. AWS recommends this option when that geographic boundary meets the workload's data-residency requirement.

source.title: Route model inference requests across AWS Regions with cross-Region inference

en.statement: An in-house RAG app on unchanged third-party FMs fits the Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix's Enterprise app scope.
en.explanation: A company-built RAG application using an existing third-party FM belongs to Scope 3: Pre-trained models. The matrix distinguishes building an application from consuming a third-party enterprise application.

source.title: Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix

en.statement: The Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix delegates consumer-app risk assessment to the app provider.
en.explanation: Organizations using consumer AI apps still assess provider risks and their own responsibilities. The matrix's security disciplines span the different use-case scopes.

source.title: Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix

en.statement: A team using a third-party FM in Amazon Bedrock reviews both AWS's terms and the model provider's terms.
en.explanation: Service terms govern use of the hosting service, while model-provider terms govern use of the model within it. AWS advises reviewing both for applications built with third-party FMs.

source.title: Securing generative AI: An introduction to the Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix

en.statement: AI teams assign a trained model the highest sensitivity classification present in the data used to train it.
en.explanation: Training can encode sensitive information in model weights. AWS advises classifying the resulting model at the highest sensitivity level used during training.

source.title: Securing generative AI: An introduction to the Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix

en.statement: The Responsible AI Lens acts as a compliance checklist for determining an AI workload's legal obligations.
en.explanation: The Responsible AI Lens offers advisory considerations for a use case. Organizations interpret their applicable legal obligations separately with legal counsel.

source.title: Responsible AI Lens: How to use this guidance
